 Thybulle's overtime steal helps Lakers win 9th straight
 Written By
 basketball.com.au
 Los Angeles Lakers’ Matisse Thybulle defends Charlotte Hornets’ Brandon Miller at Crypto.com Arena in Los Angeles on November 18, 2026 (AEDT). Photo: Adam Pantozzi/NBAE via Getty Images. Copyright 2026 NBAE.
 Share now: Highlights
 The Boomers wing struck with 8.8 seconds left in overtime as the Lakers made it nine straight wins.
 Matisse Thybulle's steal with 8.8 seconds left in overtime set up a four-point lead 
 The Lakers' nine straight wins is the NBA's longest active streak, and they are 13-2 
 Josh Green shot 4-from-5 for nine points as Utah ended a 12-game losing streak 
 Lakers wing Matisse Thybulle , 29, stole the ball with 8.8 seconds left in overtime on sideline out of bounds play to help the Los Angeles Lakers beat the Charlotte Hornets 118-114 at crypto.com Arena on Wednesday, November 18 (AEDT).
 It was the last of his three steals, and the free throw he made after it gave the Lakers a four-point lead. The win was their ninth straight, the longest active streak in the NBA once the Detroit Pistons ended the San Antonio Spurs' 12-game run on the same night. At 13-2 the Lakers also have the best record in the league, and Thybulle has started all 15 games, with 34 steals, numbers that feature in his case in our Boomers 2027 World Cup roster selector .
 Thybulle has three steals or more in six consecutive games.
 GAME OVER 😭 Matisse Thybulle really pulled off the ultimate redemption arc and snatched that game-winning steal 🔒 pic.twitter.com/iaYtVdHvGc 
— NBACodex (@Isaacococ999) November 18, 2026 
 Josh Green shot 4-from-5 for nine points as the Utah Jazz won 132-107 at the Los Angeles Clippers to end a 12-game losing streak, and Rocco Zikarsky was on the bench, a coach's decision, as the Minnesota Timberwolves beat the Portland Trail Blazers 106-105.
 Three Australians had a game and their teams went 3-0, counting Zikarsky, who was dressed but did not play. Thybulle and Green were the two who got on the floor, and both won.
 There was no game for Dyson Daniels and Jock Landale 's Atlanta Hawks, Tyrese Proctor 's Cleveland Cavaliers, Josh Giddey 's Chicago Bulls, Duop Reath 's Phoenix Suns, Kyrie Irving 's Dallas Mavericks, Ben Simmons 's Sacramento Kings or Johnny Furphy 's Indiana Pacers.
 Games played Tuesday, November 17 US time, Wednesday, November 18 AEDT. Every game involving an Australian is final. All times AEDT. Every Australian is on our Aussies in the NBA hub . 
 Los Angeles Lakers 118 Charlotte Hornets 114 (OT, Final) 
 Matisse Thybulle's late overtime steal in a Lakers win against the Hornets at crypto.com Arena on Wednesday, November 18 (AEDT) 
 Los Angeles Lakers wing Matisse Thybulle started and had seven points, six rebounds, three steals and a block in 31 minutes as the Lakers beat the Charlotte Hornets 118-114 in overtime. He shot 2-from-6, all from three, and 1-from-2 at the line, with no assists and one turnover, and finished plus-eight.
 Quentin Grimes had made two free throws for a 117-114 lead with 11.5 seconds left in overtime when Thybulle picked off Royce O'Neale's pass on Charlotte's next possession, and Liam McNeeley fouled him straight away. He missed the first free throw and made the second for 118-114, and McNeeley's three with 2.2 seconds left missed.
 The Lakers had needed a late escape just to get there, trailing 94-81 after three quarters and 110-106 with 33.1 seconds left in regulation, when Thybulle's pass went out of bounds. After Grimes' layup and a Coby White free throw, Thybulle grabbed the rebound of White's missed second shot with 12.1 seconds left, and Grimes' 26-foot three from a Luka Doncic pass tied it 111-111 with 2.4 seconds to go.
 Earlier, Thybulle stole the ball from White and hit a three from a Doncic pass in the first quarter, blocked a White floater just before the first break, and added a second three and a steal from Moussa Diabate in the second quarter, the steal coming with the Lakers ahead 55-44. It was his sixth straight game with at least three steals.
 Grimes scored 47 points with 10 threes from 14 attempts and Doncic had 36 points on 13-from-34 shooting for the 13-2 Lakers, who won their ninth straight after the eighth on November 16 . Brandon Miller scored 28 and Naz Reid had 23 points and 11 rebounds for the 4-10 Hornets, who have lost three in a row.
 Next: Utah Jazz at Los Angeles Lakers, Thursday, November 19, 2:00pm, with Thybulle and Josh Green on opposite sides.
 Utah Jazz 132 Los Angeles Clippers 107 (Final) 
 Josh Green's 4-from-5 shooting in a Jazz win against the Clippers at Intuit Dome on Wednesday, November 18 (AEDT) 
 Utah Jazz guard Josh Green, 26, started and had nine points and a rebound in 13 minutes as the Jazz beat the Los Angeles Clippers 132-107. He shot 4-from-5, 1-from-1 from three and did not go to the line, with two turnovers, and finished even.
 He scored the game's first basket with a turnaround jumper, hit a three from a Keyonte George pass for a 50-42 lead in the second quarter, and scored twice from Mo Bamba passes early in the third, the second a pull-up for 75-68. The nine points were one short of his season high of 10.
 Brice Sensabaugh scored 40 points on 16-from-21 shooting, with eight threes and 11 rebounds, and George had 30 points and 11 assists for the 2-13 Jazz, who outscored the Clippers 44-21 in the fourth quarter. Brook Lopez scored 23, and Darius Garland and Rui Hachimura 20 each, for the 4-9 Clippers.
 Next: Utah Jazz at Los Angeles Lakers, Thursday, November 19, 2:00pm.
 Minnesota Timberwolves 106 Portland Trail Blazers 105 (Final) 
 Rocco Zikarsky on the bench for a one-point Timberwolves win against the Trail Blazers at Target Center on Wednesday, November 18 (AEDT) 
 Rocco Zikarsky, 20, was in Minnesota's box score as a coach's decision and did not play as the Timberwolves beat the Portland Trail Blazers 106-105. He was not in the box score for Minnesota's previous game, against the same opponent, on November 17.
 Jaden McDaniels' running layup from an Ayo Dosunmu pass with 2.6 seconds left won it, after LaMelo Ball stole the ball from Donovan Clingan. Trey Lyles then blocked Damian Lillard's drive with 1.3 seconds left, and Toumani Camara missed a layup with 0.4 seconds left.
 Dosunmu scored 30 points with seven threes and McDaniels had 22 for the 11-4 Timberwolves. Lillard scored 25 and Jrue Holiday 23 for the 9-5 Trail Blazers.
 Next: New York Knicks at Minnesota Timberwolves, Friday, November 20, 12:00pm.
